subject: geography
title: Geopolitical Tensions and Hot Spots
welcome_lead: From the South China Sea to the Arctic, study contemporary geopolitical flashpoints.
meta_desc: IBDP Geography HL Adventure: geopolitical tensions, hot spots and contemporary risk.
final_note: You have mapped current tensions. Geography continues to shape security and cooperation.

concepts.def: Disputes between states over territory, resources, identity or influence.
Overlapping claims by China, Vietnam, Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei and Taiwan over reefs and waters.
Chinese cartographic claim covering most of the South China Sea, rejected by 2016 PCA ruling.
Intergovernmental forum of 8 Arctic states established 1996 to coordinate cooperation.
Long-running unresolved dispute with no active large-scale fighting, e.g. Nagorno-Karabakh prior to 2020.
Economic and political measures imposed on states to coerce policy change.

walkthroughs.body_html: China's nine-dash line overlaps with EEZ claims of neighbouring states. Artificial island construction on reefs like Mischief and Subi, combined with the 2016 Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling in favour of the Philippines, exemplifies legal vs power-based geopolitics.

Receding sea ice opens shipping routes (Northern Sea Route, Northwest Passage) and resource access. Russia, Canada, US, Norway, Denmark (Greenland) maintain claims; China declares itself a 'near-Arctic state'. The Arctic Council faces strains after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

Ukraine (Russian invasion 2022-), Gaza-Israel, Yemen, Sahel coups, Taiwan Strait, Kashmir, Ethiopia-Tigray (ended 2022) and the Korean peninsula illustrate diverse geopolitical risks. Climate change, scarcity and disinformation increasingly intersect with traditional drivers of conflict.
